title: Dream Finders Homes Submits Revised and Increased All-Cash Proposal to Acquire Beazer Homes for $32.00 Per Share
summary: Represents immediate cash premium of approximately 70% over Beazer’s undisturbed share price on May 8, 2026; represents nearly 24% increase to…...
body_text: Dream Finders Homes Submits Revised and Increased All-Cash Proposal to Acquire Beazer Homes for $32.00 Per Share July 08, 2026 7:00am EDT Download as PDF Represents immediate cash premium of approximately 70% over Beazer’s undisturbed share price on May 8, 2026; represents nearly 24% increase to prior public proposal Follows repeated attempts by Dream Finders to engage in good faith and multiple increased offers submitted to Beazer’s Board Dream Finders urges Beazer shareholders to encourage the Board to withdraw unreasonable preconditions and engage constructively to pursue this compelling proposal Investor presentation available at announcement.dreamfindershomes.com JACKSONVILLE, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Dream Finders Homes, Inc. (the “Company”, “Dream Finders”) (NYSE: DFH), announced today that it has submitted a revised proposal to the board of directors of Beazer Homes USA, Inc. (“Beazer”) to acquire all outstanding shares of Beazer in an all-cash transaction for $32.00 per share, a nearly 24% increase to its prior proposal dated May 5, 2026, made public May 11, 2026. This new proposal represents a premium of approximately 70% to Beazer’s undisturbed share price of $18.77 on May 8, 2026,1 and a premium of approximately 56% to Beazer’s undisturbed 30-day VWAP of $20.48 as of the same date.2 As outlined in the correspondence below, this proposal is Dream Finders’ latest attempt to engage constructively with Beazer’s management and Board (the “Beazer Board”). Prior to this most recent proposal, on June 22, 2026, Dream Finders submitted a revised all-cash offer to acquire Beazer for $29.25 per share (the “June 22 Proposal”). Following feedback from Beazer advisors, on June 30, 2026, Dream Finders submitted to the Beazer Board its revised proposal for $32.00 per share in cash (the “June 30 Proposal”). Beazer has now introduced new roadblocks by demanding onerous preconditions to commencing due diligence with Dream Finders. For example, Beazer has insisted that Dream Finders enter into a non-disclosure agreement with a 12-month standstill period (the “standstill period”). Dream Finders believes this is an attempt by Beazer to further delay engagement and impede the potential transaction. Dream Finders is making its latest proposal public following Beazer’s continued resistance to engaging constructively with Dream Finders and to offer Beazer shareholders the opportunity they deserve to evaluate this compelling proposal for themselves. Patrick Zalupski, Dream Finders’ Chairman and CEO, said, “Beazer’s actions do not appear to be focused on pursuing a path that can maximize value for shareholders. While we would have preferred to continue our discussions privately, Beazer’s proposed non-disclosure agreement and related restrictions go well beyond what is necessary to protect confidential information. Taken together with Beazer’s past unwillingness to engage, these provisions raise questions about whether the Board is prepared to pursue a transaction that we believe would be in the best interest of Beazer shareholders.” Zalupski continued, “As we’ve previously outlined, Beazer has persistently underperformed relative to peers, being the only public homebuilder reporting consecutive quarters of operating losses. Management’s strategy has not delivered for shareholders and we believe it is not suited to the current market environment. Dream Finders remains committed to pursuing this transaction and is prepared to accelerate other measures to achieve shareholders’ desired outcome.” In a new investor presentation accompanying today’s announcement, Dream Finders outlined the financial merits of the revised proposal and reaffirmed its commitment to a successful transaction: Compelling premium and value: The $32.00 per share, all-cash offer delivers highly compelling and certain value to Beazer’s shareholders. Transaction confidence: Dream Finders does not currently anticipate any regulatory or other concerns that would prevent closing the proposed transaction. Financing: Dream Finders has received letters from financial institutions confirming that they are highly confident the financing can be arranged in the capital markets. Expedited timeline: Dreams Finders is fully committed to completing the transaction and is ready to begin limited due diligence on an expedited basis and concurrently negotiate definitive acquisition agreements. For more information, visit announcement.dreamfindershomes.com . Advisors Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, BofA Securities, Zelman Partners and Vestra Advisors are acting as financial advisors to Dream Finders, Foley & Lardner is acting as legal counsel and Edelman Smithfield is acting as strategic communications advisor. Financing Kennedy Lewis has provided Dream Finders with a highly confident letter in connection with land bank financing related to the proposed transaction. Dream Finders has also obtained letters from Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC and BofA Securities stating that they are highly confident that financing for the transaction can be arranged in the capital markets. *** Dream Finders sent the following letter on June 30, 2026 , to Allan P. Merrill, Chairman, President and CEO of Beazer: Dear Mr. Merrill: I am writing to follow up on our letter dated June 22, 2026 that delivered our proposal to acquire 100% of Beazer Homes USA, Inc. (“BZH”) for $29.25 per share (the “June 22 Proposal”) in an all-cash transaction (the “Transaction”). Since the June 22 Proposal, we have received additional feedback from your advisors on a path to engaging constructively on a potential Transaction, which is reflected in this update to our June 22 Proposal. Based on the feedback received, we are pleased to submit a revised proposal to acquire 100% of BZH for $32.00 per share in an all-cash transaction (the “June 30 Proposal”). This proposal offers a significant increase to our June 22 Proposal and a 70.5% premium to BZH’s undisturbed shared price of $18.77 as of May 8, 2026. The June 30 Proposal is conditioned on the satisfactory completion of due diligence customary for a transaction of this nature, including, but not limited to, meetings with senior management; business and commercial diligence, including assessment of potential synergies and business plan by market; financial diligence, including detailed analysis of current inventory (land, land under development, lot deposits, and model homes); capital structure review, including analysis of existing debt instruments and leases; legal diligence, including review of legal entity org charts, material contracts, existing and potential litigations, and ongoing obligations of BZH’s not-for-profit arm; tax analysis, including validation of deferred tax assets; information systems review; analysis of HR and employee-related matters, including review of full corporate census and org charts; and other matters prior to the execution of a definitive agreement. We are prepared to conduct our due diligence expeditiously and will dedicate the resources to move quickly toward execution of a definitive agreement and announcement of the Transaction. The June 30 Proposal has the full support of our Board of Directors. It remains subject to customary conditions, including completion of confirmatory due diligence, final Board approval, and negotiation of mutually acceptable definitive transaction documents with customary terms and conditions for a transaction of this type. We welcome the opportunity to engage constructively and collaboratively through bilateral discussions, and we are prepared to move expeditiously to reach an agreement privately. We kindly ask that you respond to this letter by Thursday, July 2, 2026 at 5pm Eastern. Thank you for your consideration. Very truly yours, Patrick O. Zalupski CEO and Chairman of the Board *** Dream Finders sent the following letter on June 22, 2026 , to Allan P. Merrill, Chairman, President and CEO of Beazer: Dear Mr. Merrill: I am writing to follow up on your press release from May 11, 2026, in which you rejected our proposal to acquire 100% of Beazer Homes USA, Inc. (“BZH”) for $25.75 per share (the “Prior Proposal”) in an all-cash transaction (the “Transaction”). Since we put forward our Prior Proposal, we have engaged meaningfully and constructively with a significant number of your shareholders, while advancing our analysis of BZH and engaging with our own shareholders. We have been highly encouraged by the feedback the shareholders of both companies have provided, which underscores broad recognition that a combination of our two companies has the potential to deliver compelling value for all stakeholders. We have also been in discussions with other interested parties on mutually beneficial arrangements that facilitate and enhance the financing and execution of the Transaction. In light of the shareholder support we have received and our continued conviction in the strategic and financial merits of a transaction, we are pleased to submit a revised proposal of $29.25 per share in cash (the “Revised Proposal”), which sits at the high end of our valuation range, based on the outside-in information we currently have. This Revised Proposal delivers a 13.6% increase to our Prior Proposal and a 55.8% premium to BZH’s undisturbed share price of $18.77 on May 8, 2026. We are confident that our Revised Proposal is highly compelling, offers significant and certain value to, and would be embraced by your shareholders. The terms of our Revised Proposal are follows: Holders of BZH common stock will receive an aggregate consideration of $29.25 per share in cash, which represents a premium of 55.8% to BZH’s undisturbed share price of $18.77 on May 8, 2026, and a premium of 42.1% to BZH’s undisturbed 30-day VWAP of $20.58 as of the same date. We believe our Revised Proposal maximizes transaction value and certainty for BZH’s shareholders. We expect to finance the Transaction with committed financing from Kennedy Lewis (“KL”), Goldman Sachs and Bank of America. Please find enclosed highly confident letters from KL (Exhibit A), Goldman Sachs (Exhibit B) and Bank of America (Exhibit C). We are prepared to complete our due diligence expeditiously and will dedicate the resources required to move quickly toward execution of a definitive agreement and announcement of the Transaction. To that end, we have retained Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, Zelman & Associates and Vestra Advisors as financial advisors; Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP and Foley & Lardner LLP as legal counsel; and Kennedy Lewis as our land-banking advisor in connection with the Transaction. We are confident in our ability to obtain any regulatory and other approvals required to consummate the Transaction. The Dream Finders Homes Inc. (“DFH”) Board of Directors supports this Revised Proposal. This non-binding Revised Proposal remains subject to customary conditions, including completion of confirmatory due diligence, final Board approval, and negotiation of mutually acceptable definitive transaction documents. We expect the definitive agreement to contain customary terms and conditions for a transaction of this type. Our Revised Proposal is submitted on the understanding that its contents will be kept confidential, subject to applicable securities laws, and that no binding obligations will arise unless and until the parties execute a definitive agreement. We propose that BZH and DFH enter into a 30-day exclusivity agreement to allow DFH to complete its due diligence and negotiate definitive agreements. We welcome the opportunity to engage constructively and collaboratively through bilateral discussions and to reach an agreement privately. We believe that engagement at the price in our Revised Proposal is in the best interests of BZH shareholders, and we are prepared to move expeditiously to advance a transaction. In the absence of meaningful and constructive engagement, we intend to take our Revised Proposal back to shareholders and accelerate other measures to achieve shareholders’ desired outcome. We kindly ask that you respond to this letter by Monday, June 29, 2026 at 5pm Eastern. Thank you for your consideration. Very truly yours, Patrick O. Zalupski CEO and Chairman of the Board About Dream Finders Homes Dream Finders Homes (NYSE: DFH), headquartered in Jacksonville, Florida, was recognized as the 2025 National Builder of the Year by Builder magazine. Dream Finders Homes builds single-family homes throughout the Southeast, Mid-Atlantic and Midwest, including Florida, Texas, Tennessee, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Colorado, Arizona, and the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area, which comprises Washington D.C., Northern Virginia and Maryland. As the Official Home Builder of the PGA TOUR, the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Tampa Bay Rays, Dream Finders Homes is deeply committed to excellence beyond homebuilding and into the communities it serves. Through its wholly owned subsidiaries, DFH also provides mortgage financing as well as title agency and underwriting services to homebuyers. Dream Finders Homes achieves its growth and returns by maintaining an asset-light homebuilding model. For more information, please visit www.dreamfindershomes.com . title: What is Fleet Management?
summary: Use fleet management software to optimize your fleet of vehicles with vehicle tracking and a reliable management system for better performance.
body_text: Fleet management is the system and processes required to operate and optimize a fleet of vehicles. Organizations use fleet management software to increase the overall function and capabilities of their commercial vehicles. Fleet fuel management allows organizations to track performance and monitor any fleet maintenance to boost overall productivity and keep operations running smoothly. How Fleet Management Works Fleet management combines real-time tracking, analytics, and decision-making to help fleet managers reduce fleet costs, improve efficiency, and maintain consistent performance across a fleet of vehicles. Step 1: Data Collection (GPS and Telematics) Fleet systems collect data from GPS tracking and telematics devices installed in vehicles. This includes vehicle location, fuel usage, idle time, and vehicle usage patterns. Real-time data allows fleet managers to track vehicle movement, monitor driver activity, and maintain visibility across operations. Step 2: Analysis Collected data is processed into usable insights through analytics and reporting tools. Fleet managers evaluate key metric indicators such as fuel costs, route efficiency, and maintenance schedules to identify trends and inefficiencies. This step helps prioritize areas that require attention. Step 3: Decision-Making Based on insights, fleet managers make informed decisions to improve performance. This can include adjusting dispatch routes, optimizing vehicle acquisition strategies, or addressing excessive idle time. Data-driven decisions help ensure resources are used efficiently across fleet operations. Step 4: Optimization Fleet management systems help automate ongoing improvements by continuously monitoring performance. Over time, fleets can reduce fuel consumption, improve vehicle usage, and streamline operations. Optimization ensures long-term efficiency and cost control without requiring constant manual oversight. What Do Fleet Managers Do? Managers who look after their fleet’s operations maximize the fleet’s efficiency in key areas, including: ‍ Fuel consumption Vehicle maintenance Utilization of assets Route planning Waste reduction Managing driver behavior and their vehicles ‍ Keeping every element of a fleet functioning at full capacity boosts effectiveness, cuts down operational costs, and reduces waste. Plus, leveraging the power of vehicle telematics provides additional opportunities to analyze key pieces of data. ‍ {{CTA}} ‍ Responsibilities of a Fleet Manager A fleet manager can have a wide range of roles and responsibilities to help a fleet run smoothly. With many moving parts, having a dedicated manager to monitor, evaluate, and upgrade areas such as cost reduction, safety, and tracking will have a critical impact. ‍ Here are a few of the primary tasks a fleet manager is responsible for: Fleet tracking —Knowing where drivers are at all times ensures driver safety. Yet, whether it is a few vehicles or a fleet of hundreds, it can often be a challenging task to accurately track each one. Fleet managers leverage the power of GPS tools and tracking systems for efficient operations. Driver safety —Putting proper guidelines in place to keep drivers safe is essential to fleet success, and fleet managers use the likes of vehicle tracking systems and dash cams for real-time visibility. This can be especially important since drivers often travel long distances. Cost Reduction —Finding ways to reduce fleet expenses frees up cash flow for other opportunities. Everything from fuel cost, maintenance, and operational costs can add up. A fleet manager will explore cost-saving solutions that will ultimately lead to efficient operations. ‍ Key Components of Fleet Management Systems Each component plays a role in improving visibility, reducing fleet costs, and maintaining control across a fleet of vehicles. Telematics Telematics systems collect and transmit data from vehicles, including speed, location, and performance metrics. This data provides real-time insights that help fleet managers monitor operations and improve decision-making. GPS Tracking GPS tracking enables fleet managers to track vehicle movement and monitor vehicle location in real time. This improves dispatch efficiency and supports better route planning across daily operations. Fuel Management Fuel management focuses on monitoring fuel usage and identifying opportunities to reduce fuel costs. By analyzing fueling patterns and driver behavior, fleets can improve efficiency and reduce unnecessary expenses. Maintenance Systems Maintenance systems track vehicle health and manage maintenance schedules. Staying ahead of maintenance needs helps reduce downtime, extend asset life, and improve reliability. Compliance Tools Compliance tools help fleets meet regulatory requirements related to safety, reporting, and operations. These systems ensure fleet managers maintain consistency across all vehicles and avoid disruptions. Driver Management Driver management focuses on improving performance and safety through data and visibility. Monitoring driver behavior helps reduce risk, improve efficiency, and support better decision-making across fleet operations. Benefits of Effective Fleet Management Proper fleet management systems can impact an entire organization by enhancing driver performance, safety protocols, productivity, and profit. ‍ A few additional benefits of a fleet management solution include: ‍ A boost in efficiency – Keeping vehicles on the road for longer and operating at their maximum capacity contributes to an efficient, streamlined operation. You can extend the lifespan of your vehicles, improve fuel efficiency, and reduce your organization’s carbon footprint. ‍ An increase in profitability – A well-oiled fleet that is optimized to drive for longer will see a rise in profitability and a drop in expenses. When you can reduce costs in areas like maintenance by staying on top of vehicle needs, you can take your investments to a new level by expanding business operations. ‍ An upgrade in safety – Regular maintenance and inspection of fleet vehicles ensures they are kept in tip-top shape. Potential issues can be detected earlier which will provide opportunities to significantly reduce the possibility of breakdowns. ‍ An upswing in compliance – Fleet management includes the need to be compliant with various regulatory requirements. Not keeping up-to-date or on top of these obligations can lead to fines and impact areas such as cash flow. ‍ ‍ An improvement in overall service – Operating an entire fleet of vehicles likely means you deliver services and orders to customers. Fulfilling customer needs effectively and efficiently is integral to business success. When your customers have positive experiences, their confidence and trust in what you offer will grow, leading to a deeper sense of loyalty. ‍ What Is Fleet Management Software? Fleet management software is a centralized platform that helps fleet managers monitor, analyze, and optimize fleet operations. It integrates data from multiple systems to provide a complete view of performance across a fleet of vehicles. Software can help automate tasks such as dispatch, reporting, and maintenance tracking, reducing manual work and improving accuracy. It also enables fleet managers to track vehicle location, monitor fuel usage, and manage maintenance schedules from a single system. By combining analytics, automation, and real-time visibility, fleet management software helps organizations reduce fuel costs, improve operational efficiency, and maintain better control over fleet performance. As fleets grow, software becomes essential for managing complexity and scaling operations effectively. ‍ {{CTA}} ‍ Experience the Power of a Fuel Card Accepted Nationwide with AtoB Effective fleet management is essential for finding ways to reduce costs and keep drivers driving. It benefits both your business and the customers you serve, and AtoB has what you need to keep your drivers on the road for longer with our next-generation fuel card. ‍ It also covers a range of expenses, from insurance, repairs, tolls, and more, and is powered by Mastercard technology, meaning it is accepted across a broad network of fuel locations. title: Inside Elastic InfoSec's agentic SOC: When to inline your agent's skills for a 5× cost reduction
summary: See the data behind a 5.7x cost cut in Elastic's agentic SOC: $0.69 vs $3.42 per alert, from 36,822 real Agent Builder conversations.
body_text: 24 July 2026 • Aaron Jewitt Inside Elastic InfoSec's agentic SOC: When to inline your agent's skills for a 5× cost reduction We tested two agentic SOC architectures in parallel across 36,822 real Agent Builder conversations. One won by 5.7x: a specialized workflow triaging alerts for $0.69 each, against $3.42 for a single agent juggling 14 Skills. The data and the decision framework are both below. 10 min read Generative AI , Detection Engineering This is Part 2 of the Inside Elastic InfoSec's Agentic SOC series. Part 1: How we triage every alert before an analyst opens it . Part 3: how we cut AI agent LLM calls by 60% . Investigating a Windows endpoint alert in Elastic InfoSec's production agentic security operations center (SOC) costs $0.69. That's what we pay running an orchestration workflow of specialized Elastic AI agents on the Elastic Inference Service (EIS). Route the same alert to a single agent working through 14 skills , and the bill jumps to $3.42, 5.7x more. At 100 investigations a day, that's an $8,000 monthly gap, and we didn't get it from a lab. It came out of 36,822 real Elastic Agent Builder conversations running in our own production environment. The gap comes down to how you build the SOC in the first place. Give one broad agent a library of skills, and it loads whatever it needs on the fly. Build a fleet of specialized agents instead, and each one runs a fixed methodology through an orchestration layer. Agent Builder handles either setup fine. At our volume, though, running the unoptimized configuration for batch triage is exactly what turns into that $8,000 a month. We'll walk through why the gap opens up, when each architecture earns its keep, and how you can run this same comparison on your own alerts. Multiple specialized agents versus a single agent with skills The single agent with skills is one broad agent paired with a library of Agent Builder skills . The agent has a thin system prompt that describes its general purpose and lists 14 skills it can invoke: macOS forensics, Windows forensics, AWS CloudTrail, Okta investigation, and others. When a new alert or analyst question arrives, the agent decides which skills are relevant, loads them on demand, and reasons over the result. No routing layer, no separate agents. One agent, one context window, one conversation. The single-agent approach is also significantly simpler to build. For teams that aren’t yet ready to invest in a full multi-agent workflow, it’s a practical starting point: Deploy a single agent with skills, scope it to critical severity alerts only, and get agentic investigation coverage running quickly. As your team builds familiarity with Agent Builder and capacity to maintain specialized agents, you can graduate your highest-volume investigation types into the specialized workflow, while the skills agent remains the front door for everything else. Skills aren’t inefficient. They’re loaded on demand, which is exactly what you want when a human analyst is exploring an alert and may need to pivot in unexpected directions. An analyst who starts with macOS forensics, discovers a lateral movement indicator, and needs to pull in the Okta investigation skill next benefits from that on-demand loading. It’s the right behavior for a conversation-driven workflow. The specialized agent workflow is built around a deterministic orchestration layer and a fleet of specialized agents. An Elastic workflow fires when an alert is generated. It enriches the alert with data from 15 or more sources using Elasticsearch Query Language (ES|QL) queries, runs infrastructure checks that close low-risk alerts with no AI cost, and routes the surviving alert to an initial triage agent that makes a first-pass verdict. If the initial triage agent is uncertain, the workflow opens a Kibana case and dispatches a set of specialized agents, each scoped to one domain. The macOS forensics agent knows exactly which tools to use, in what order, with what stop criteria. That methodology is written directly into its system prompt. It doesn’t browse a library of methodologies at runtime; it runs one methodology, deterministically, every time. A Final Review agent reads the findings from all the specialized agents and writes the analyst-facing verdict. For the full pipeline walkthrough, see our companion post Part 1: How we triage every alert before an analyst opens it . Both architectures use the same underlying platform: Agent Builder for agent construction and deployment, Elastic Workflows for orchestration in the specialized workflow, and Elastic Inference Service (EIS) for large language model (LLM) inference. The difference is where investigation methodology lives: written inline across many specialized agents, or loaded on demand into one general agent. Customer Zero: How Elastic InfoSec runs Agent Builder in its own production SOC At Elastic, our InfoSec team operates as Customer Zero. We run the newest versions of Elastic Security and Agent Builder in our production environment, often before they reach general availability, across a globally distributed fleet of laptops, servers, and cloud workloads. We’re the first and most demanding user of every feature we ship. The numbers in this post aren’t a benchmark we built for the blog. They come from 36,822 real conversations across our production and QA Agent Builder deployments, totaling about 8 billion tokens. Roughly 99.3% of all agent executions ran on Claude Sonnet 4.5 via EIS. The architectural question we answer here is one we had to answer ourselves, as our monthly EIS bill started to climb quickly. How do you measure per-agent token cost in Agent Builder? Agent Builder exposes a consumption endpoint that returns token usage by agent over any time range: curl -X POST \ -H "Authorization: ApiKey ${KIBANA_API_KEY}" \ -H 'kbn-xsrf: true' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ "${KIBANA_URL}/s/${KIBANA_SPACE}/api/agent_builder/agents/${AGENT_ID}/consumption" \ -d '{"from":"2026-04-01T00:00:00Z","to":"2026-05-01T00:00:00Z"}' Replace ${KIBANA_URL} , ${KIBANA_API_KEY} , ${KIBANA_SPACE} , and ${AGENT_ID} with your Kibana URL, API key, space name, and target agent ID. The response includes: conversations : Total conversation count in the range. tokens.input : Total input tokens consumed. tokens.output : Total output tokens consumed. Per-model breakdown, so you can verify which model is actually in use. The time range echoed back for confirmation. The API returns totals and statistical summaries (including median) for the period. It doesn’t return per-conversation traces. That makes it straightforward to track fleet-level costs over time, but harder to measure what a single investigation actually costs. To close that gap, we ran matched-live experiments: the same alert, submitted to both architectures in sequence, with the output of each run recorded independently. Per-investigation cost for the specialized workflow is a composed estimate, not a single call measurement. Each specialized agent runs in its own context. We sum the median token counts of the specialized agents involved in a route, plus the Final Review agent, to get the per-route median. These route estimates are consistent with our matched-live Windows and Higher-Order threshold runs. Token cost by investigation route Specialized agents columns use median per-agent token counts from the consumption API, summed across the agents in each route (hundreds to thousands of conversations per agent). Single agent with on-demand skills columns show the average tokens used across our matched runs. Investigation route Specialized agents Single agent Token ratio Endpoint Windows ~113k ~649k 5.7× Higher-Order threshold alert ~243k ~722k ~3.0× The Windows and Higher-Order threshold pairs are matched-live measurements: the same alert submitted to both architectures. The specialized workflow route totals are composed estimates (sum of per-agent medians) consistent with those matched runs. At EIS rates for Claude Sonnet 4.5, those token counts translate directly to dollars. Current rates are on the EIS pricing page . Cost includes EIS inference charges plus Elastic Agent Builder execution metering ($0.025 per execution on Serverless; each 50,000 input tokens count as one additional execution beyond the base interaction). Investigation route Specialized agents cost Single agent cost Savings per investigation Endpoint Windows $0.69 $3.42 $2.73 Higher-Order threshold alert $1.48 $3.82 $2.34 At scale, that per-investigation difference compounds quickly. Monthly figures below extrapolate from the Windows-route cost ($0.69 specialized versus $3.42 single agent); replace with your own per-route cost to estimate your spend. Daily volume Specialized agents / month Single agent / month Monthly savings 100 / day $2,070 $10,260 $8,190 500 / day $10,350 $51,300 $40,950 1,000 / day $20,700 $102,600 $81,900 The single-agent token counts vary substantially across runs: from 218k to 786k in our sample of five unified-agent investigations. That variance is itself a signal. As the matched test in the next section shows, even the same alert investigated by the same agent can take different paths, depending on how many skills get invoked and how many reasoning-only LLM calls the agent makes before committing to a tool call. Inline methodology versus a skill-delegated agent: A matched test To isolate the effect of skills specifically, we ran a tighter experiment. We picked four macOS alerts that only required a single skill to investigate and sent each one to both architectures: the macOS forensics agent from the specialized workflow (methodology inline), and the same single agent with 14 skills. The numbers below are averages across the four matched runs per architecture. Metric Specialized agent (inline methodology) Test agent (skill-delegated) LLM calls 4 12 Total tokens 43,333 346,767 EIS cost (Claude Sonnet 4.5) $0.23 $1.65 Wall-clock time 41 seconds 148 seconds Process ancestry traced 100% (4 of 4) 50% (2 of 4) Reasoning-only LLM calls ~25% ~57–60% The inline agent uses 8× fewer tokens and 3.6× less wall-clock time, and it ran identically across all four runs. The skill-delegated agent followed a different investigation path on each run. Two of the four runs traced process ancestry correctly; the other two took a cheaper path that skipped that step and produced a shallower result. Same setup, different paths, driven by nondeterministic tool selection. The reasoning-only LLM call rate explains a large portion of the cost difference. About 57–60% of the skill-delegated agent's LLM calls were pure deliberation, with no new tools called and no new evidence gathered. Those LLM calls still pay the full, growing conversation-history cost. The inline agent spent only 25% of its LLM calls in reasoning, because the prompt told it what to do next. Disclaimer: The macOS matched test used four matched alerts, one run per architecture per alert. Sample size is small. The Windows and Higher-Order threshold observations used five unified-agent runs versus hundreds to thousands of specialized agent runs. These results are internally consistent, but a larger controlled experiment would tighten the confidence intervals. Treat the ratios as directionally correct, not laboratory precision. Why does on-demand skill loading cost more at scale? We found during testing that the biggest predictor of total token usage in an agentic investigation is the number of LLM calls the agent makes, not the size of its system prompt. Every LLM call pays the full, growing conversation-history cost, so each extra deliberation step multiplies the bytes already in play. In our investigations, average input tokens per LLM call held steady at roughly 36,000 tokens, regardless of system prompt size, with the growing conversation history doing most of the work. This produces a counterintuitive result: A longer, more detailed system prompt often reduces total token cost, because spelling out the methodology eliminates the LLM calls the agent would otherwise spend deciding what to do next. That insight is the main reason a workflow of specialized agents costs less at scale than a single agent with skills. The optimization workflow we use to identify and reduce these reasoning-only LLM calls in production agents is covered in Part 3 . Skills in Agent Builder are loaded on demand, not pre-injected into the agent's context. When an agent invokes a skill, it reads the skill file at runtime. That read costs one LLM call and adds the skill's content (typically 600–1,500 tokens) to the conversation context, where it stays for every subsequent LLM call. If an investigation requires three skills, the agent pays three LLM calls just to load the skills before any forensic work begins. Those skill bytes sit in the growing context window for every remaining LLM call, including all the reasoning-only LLM calls that follow. The result is compound cost: load overhead up front, plus heavier context on every LLM call that comes after. The problem is when that same flexibility runs hundreds of times a day on the same class of alert. Automated endpoint triage on macOS endpoints always follows the same path: Check the alert. Trace the process ancestry. Run two ES|QL queries. Write the verdict. There’s no exploration. The flexibility is overhead you pay for without using, every single time. Writing the methodology inline eliminates the load step. More importantly, it eliminates the deliberation. The model doesn’t need to reason about which tool to pick when the prompt tells it: Use execute_esql on kibana.alert.uuid , and then call endpoint.process_entity_id once or twice, stop. That constraint is why the inline agent runs four LLM calls and the skill-delegated agent runs 12. How to pick your agentic SOC architecture: A decision framework Which architecture to pick should follow from what you’re trying to do with each part of your SOC. Need Specialized agent workflow Single agent with skills Automated triage at hundreds of alerts per day Right tool. 3–5.7× cheaper per investigation; consistent depth Higher cost at scale; variance in depth across runs Forensic-depth reproducibility on identical input 100% process ancestry traced (4 of 4 runs) 50% process ancestry traced (2 of 4 runs); different paths across runs Token cost per investigation ~113k–243k, depending on route ~532k–786k across our five observed unified-agent runs Interactive analyst chat over one alert Mismatched for this use case; routing and specialization add friction where flexibility helps Right tool. Analyst can steer; skills load on demand as the conversation evolves (experiential, not yet measured at scale) Time to add a new domain Build a new narrow agent; update the workflow to add logic and error handling for the new agent Author one new skill; existing agent picks it up immediately Methodology change ergonomics Edit each agent's system prompt Edit one skill file; every agent that invokes it picks up the change Observability of why a decision happened Linear and predictable: enrichment, specialized agent finding, Final Review verdict Variable: Skill choices at runtime determine the path Run both when your SOC does both things. These architectures aren’t mutually exclusive, and they can coexist in the same Agent Builder deployment. Automated batch triage runs on the specialized workflow. Analyst-led interactive investigation runs on the single-agent approach. Different jobs, different shapes. Use the specialized workflow when you automate the same investigation type repeatedly and need cost control, reproducibility, and auditability. Alert triage running hundreds of times a day on the same rule class is the canonical case. Maintaining one agent per domain adds overhead compared to a single agent, but the cost savings at scale offset that quickly. At 500 endpoint investigations per day, a 5× cost difference isn’t a rounding error. Use the single agent with skills when the investigation is analyst-led and the direction may shift mid-conversation. On-demand skill loading is a feature in that context, not a cost. The analyst can start with macOS forensics, discover an anomalous Okta login, and pivot to identity investigation without switching interfaces or writing a new query. Measure before you decide. The per-agent consumption API makes this tractable even before you commit to a design. Deploy both approaches in a QA environment, run each against the same set of representative alerts, and sum the median token costs by route. Your numbers will differ from ours, depending on your alert mix, your methodology depth, and which models your connectors use. But the measurement approach is the same. What Elastic InfoSec runs in production today The specialized agent workflow runs in production for automated alert triage at Elastic InfoSec. Every alert from our detection rules passes through the workflow, gets enriched by ES|QL queries, and routes to the appropriate specialized agents before an analyst opens it. For the full pipeline walkthrough, see Part 1: How we triage every alert before an analyst opens it . The single agent with skills is available in our environment for analyst-led investigation. It handles conversational pivots and follow-on questions in ways the specialized workflow does not, and it gives the analyst flexibility to investigate a single alert, work across multiple domains in one session, hunt threats using indicators, or generate an executive summary for a case. Specialized agents versus skills: The bottom line for your agentic SOC For agentic automations that you run hundreds of times a day, building specialized agents with inlined skills cuts token cost 3–5.7x, increases efficiency, and improves the consistency of your analysis. For human-led, exploratory, cross-domain work the skills-based agent is the right shape, and it’s the easiest way to get started. The broader principle is worth keeping as you design your SOC: Match architecture to use case, and measure before you assume. An architecture that works well for one part of your SOC may be the wrong shape for another. The consumption API gives you the data to make that call on your own alerts, with your own agent configurations, rather than relying on numbers from a different environment. If you’re standing up an agentic SOC on Elastic, start with the Agent Builder documentation and the Workflows documentation . Run the consumption API against your own deployments, and tell us what you find. title: From Brief to Buy: How Butler/Till Used DV Neura to Embed Verification Into Agentic Workflows
summary: In this blog, learn how Butler/Till used DV Neura to embed verification into agentic workflows, allowing for campaigns to scale easily.
body_text: By Ben Cann, Senior Vice President of Product Management, DoubleVerify Setting up and executing digital advertising campaigns has never been simple. Advertisers must balance performance, inventory quality, brand suitability, fraud protection and compliance requirements while coordinating decisions across multiple platforms and partners. The growing use of curated inventory, private marketplace (PMP) and programmatic guaranteed (PG) deals has added another layer of complexity. While these approaches provide greater control, transparency and access to premium inventory, they also require advertisers to ensure that the appropriate protections, targeting criteria and campaign requirements are consistently applied throughout planning, buying and activation workflows. For Butler/Till, a leading agency serving pharmaceutical, medtech and wellness brands, those challenges are especially important. In healthcare advertising, brand protection is not optional. Advertisers must ensure campaigns appear in appropriate environments while meeting strict compliance requirements. By combining agentic AI, emerging interoperability standards such as MCP and AdCP, with DV Neura ™ , DoubleVerify's cognitive engine that powers its platform, Butler/Till has transformed what was once a fragmented, multi-step process into a more connected workflow that brings planning, verification and activation together without compromising on protection or control. The Challenge: Translating Strategy into Execution Butler/Till has more than 25 years of experience serving healthcare advertisers, whose brand suitability and compliance needs often demand additional scrutiny. Historically, translating a campaign brief into the appropriate brand suitability, fraud protection and optimization settings required planners to navigate multiple platforms and rely on expertise that often sat outside the buying workflow itself. A planner might develop a media strategy in one platform, consult verification experts in another, activate through a separate buying environment and then manually ensure that the appropriate protections and controls were carried through to execution. While effective, the process often depended on institutional knowledge, multiple handoffs and manual validation. As campaign complexity increased, Butler/Till sought opportunities to streamline workflows while maintaining the governance and quality standards required by healthcare advertisers. “Healthcare marketers operate in some of the most complex advertising environments, where every decision must balance performance, compliance, brand suitability and consumer trust,” said Gina Whelehan, Group Director of Strategic Partnerships at Butler/Till. “Bringing verification into the workflow earlier helps our teams move faster while maintaining the governance and accountability required in highly regulated categories.” The Agentic Approach Today, Butler/Till is using Claude as its buyer agent to discover, evaluate, select and activate media buys agentically through the AdCP protocol. By connecting Claude to DoubleVerify's Media AdVantage Platform (DV MAP ™ ) via MCP, Butler/Till can feed brand preferences and verification expertise directly into the planning process and layer protection onto the agentic buy. This transforms what was once a fragmented workflow spanning multiple systems into a single guided conversation. How it Works: When a campaign brief is loaded, the conversational interface immediately surfaces brand suitability recommendations and insights tailored to both the agency trader and the brands they represent. Recommendations are layered across multiple levels, from Authentic Brand Suitability profiles that reflect a brand's specific preferences to agency-level profiles that capture best practices to off-the-shelf suitability controls aligned to particular industries or topics, such as negative news related to healthcare. This approach reflects DV's flexibility for agencies managing multiple clients and profiles, each with their own suitability requirements, standards and compliance considerations. Rather than replacing planner judgment, the system acts as a guide. It explains available options, provides context for why they may be relevant and enables planners to make informed decisions while maintaining full control over campaign settings. The workflow extends beyond brand suitability. Additional protections and performance controls, including fraud and invalid traffic avoidance, viewability thresholds and contextual alignment options, are available as optional add-ons within the same conversation, not a separate workflow. What once required multiple systems, vendor calls and manual cross-checks can now happen within a single Claude session. Early implementations indicate that integrating verification earlier in the workflow can reduce manual validation requirements and improve consistency across campaign execution. Once planning is complete, the buyer agent communicates its decisions directly to PubMatic's AgenticOS, which applies the selected protections to inventory packages before the auction and executes the campaign only on inventory that meets the selected DV criteria. Powered by DV Neura This workflow is powered by DV Neura™ , DoubleVerify's cognitive engine embedded across the DV Media AdVantage Platform. DV Neura makes DV's media intelligence, recommendations and protections available directly within AI-driven workflows. In Butler/Till's case, that allows Claude to surface relevant brand suitability, fraud protection and media quality recommendations that flow directly into PubMatic's AgenticOS where the campaign executes on inventory aligned with those protections. Once a campaign is live, those same workflows can be used to evaluate campaign quality and effectiveness. Teams can review performance, identify potential sources of waste and make informed adjustments without leaving the environment where planning and activation decisions were originally made. For agencies managing highly regulated brands, maintaining this continuity across planning, activation and optimization can help improve operational consistency while preserving necessary oversight. More broadly, Butler/Till's implementation illustrates DV's vision for the future. The company has spent years building the integrations needed to make verification available across the digital advertising ecosystem. With DV Neura, that foundation now enables something larger: trusted media intelligence that can be accessed by agents anywhere across planning, activation, optimization and measurement workflows. From Institutional Knowledge to Operational Intelligence The result is a more connected, streamlined and completely auditable process from brief to activation. Every decision can be traced back to campaign requirements, creating a clear link between advertiser objectives and the protections ultimately applied. While efficiency is a meaningful benefit, the larger opportunity is consistency. Campaigns become easier to scale, governance becomes easier to maintain and critical expertise becomes more consistently applied throughout the workflow rather than relying on a series of manual handoffs across specialists and tools. For Butler/Till, agentic AI helps teams apply healthcare media expertise, governance standards and campaign requirements more consistently and efficiently throughout the planning and activation process. As the industry moves toward more automated and agent-driven workflows, this shift goes beyond incremental improvement. It represents a fundamentally different approach to planning and activating media.

title: Cue Biopharma Announces $50.0 Million Private Placement
summary: BOSTON, July 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cue Biopharma, Inc. (Nasdaq: CUE), a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing...
body_text: BOSTON, July 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cue Biopharma, Inc. (Nasdaq: CUE), a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing transformative therapies targeting functional cures for immunological disorders, today announced that it has entered into a securities purchase agreement with a group of accredited investors for the private placement of (i) 1,418,071 shares of common stock at a purchase price of $33.21 per share and (ii) to certain investors, in lieu of shares of common stock, pre-funded warrants to purchase up to 87,500 shares of common stock at a price per pre-funded warrant of $33.209, for gross proceeds of approximately $50.0 million. The private placement is expected to close on or about July 13, 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions. The pre-funded warrants will have an exercise price of $0.001 per share, be immediately exercisable, and remain exercisable until exercised in full. The private placement was led by Cormorant Asset Management, with participation from additional new investment funds including Columbia Threadneedle Investments. title: Alinea Invest — How to Use an Investment App for Beginners: A Step by Step Guide
summary: To use an investment app as a beginner, download a regulated app such as Alinea, complete a short onboarding questionnaire about your goals and risk tolerance, link your bank account, and fund your account with any amount, even a few dollars. body_text: Quick Answer To use an investment app as a beginner, download a regulated app such as Alinea, complete a short onboarding questionnaire about your goals and risk tolerance, link your bank account, and fund your account with any amount, even a few dollars. From there, choose an expert built portfolio or automated investing plan, set up recurring deposits, and check in periodically as the app manages the details. Most beginners are fully set up and invested in under 15 minutes. Key Takeaways Investment apps let beginners open an account, fund it, and start investing from a phone in minutes, often with as little as $1 through fractional shares. The core workflow is the same on most apps: create an account, link a bank, fund it, choose investments, and automate contributions. Look for apps registered with the SEC and backed by SIPC protected brokerage accounts before depositing money. Automated and expert guided options, like Alinea's Investment Playlists and AI Copilot Allie, remove the research burden that stops most beginners from starting. Consistency matters more than timing. Small, regular, automated contributions are the most reliable habit a new investor can build. What Is an Investment App? Definition: An investment app is a mobile application that lets you open a brokerage account, deposit money, and buy assets such as stocks, exchange traded funds (ETFs), and cryptocurrencies directly from your phone. Many modern apps also include automated portfolio management, educational content, and AI powered guidance designed for first time investors. Investment apps fall into three broad categories. Self directed apps let you pick every stock yourself. Robo advisors invest automatically based on an algorithm. Hybrid platforms, such as Alinea, combine automation with expert built portfolios and human support, which is often the most comfortable starting point for beginners. Why Beginners Start With an Investing App Investing apps solve the three problems that keep most people on the sidelines: high minimums, confusing jargon, and not knowing what to buy. Fractional investing means you can own a slice of a company for a dollar instead of paying full share price. Plain language explanations replace finance speak. And curated portfolios answer the "what do I actually buy" question for you. Starting early matters because of compounding, where the returns your investments generate begin generating returns of their own. The longer your money stays invested, the more that effect works in your favor, which is why financial educators consistently emphasize time in the market over timing the market. How to Use an Investment App in 7 Steps Step 1: Choose a beginner friendly, regulated app Before anything else, verify the app is legitimate. Check that the platform is registered with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and that brokerage accounts carry SIPC protection. Alinea, for example, is an SEC registered investment advisor, and brokerage accounts on Alinea are powered by DriveWealth, a member of FINRA and SIPC, which protects accounts up to $500,000, including $250,000 for cash claims. Beyond regulation, compare fees, minimums, educational resources, and whether the app offers guidance or expects you to make every decision alone. Step 2: Download the app and complete onboarding Create your account and answer the onboarding questionnaire. Expect questions about your income, financial goals, timeline, and how you would react if your investments temporarily dropped in value. Answer honestly. On platforms like Alinea, these answers shape the portfolios you are shown, so accurate inputs lead to a plan that actually fits you. You will also verify your identity with basic personal information, a standard legal requirement for opening any brokerage account in the United States. Step 3: Link your bank account Most investment apps connect to your bank through Plaid, the same secure service used by Venmo and other major financial apps. You log in through an encrypted connection, and the app never sees or stores your banking credentials. Once linked, you can move money between your bank and your investment account in a few taps. Step 4: Decide how much to invest and fund your account Start with an amount you will not need for daily expenses. A common guideline is to keep three to six months of living costs in an emergency fund before investing, then direct a portion of what remains toward your investment account. Thanks to fractional shares, the entry point is low: on Alinea you can start with as little as $1. The amount matters less than the habit. Many beginners begin with $10 to $50 per month and increase contributions as their income grows. Step 5: Choose your investments or let the app choose for you This is where beginner friendly design pays off. Instead of researching individual tickers, you can select a pre built, diversified portfolio. Alinea calls these Investment Playlists: curated collections of stocks and ETFs built by investment experts around goals and themes, from broad market diversification to values based investing. If you have questions along the way, Alinea's AI Copilot Allie explains what you own and why in plain language, and human advisors are available for bigger picture financial questions. Tip: Diversification, spreading your money across many companies and asset types rather than one or two stocks, is the single most important risk management concept for a new investor. Pre built portfolios handle this automatically. Step 6: Set up automated recurring investing Automation is the feature that turns intention into results. Choose an amount and a schedule, weekly or monthly, and the app invests for you without any further action. This approach, called dollar cost averaging, means you buy at many different price points over time instead of trying to guess the perfect moment, which smooths out the effect of market swings and removes emotion from the process. Step 7: Monitor, learn, and stay consistent Check your portfolio periodically, but resist the urge to react to daily movement. Markets fluctuate constantly; long term investors are rewarded for patience, not activity. Use the app's educational tools to build knowledge as you go. Alinea's daily briefings summarize what is happening in the market and in your portfolio specifically, and short lessons build financial literacy over time. The goal is quiet confidence, not constant checking. What You Can Invest In Through an App Stocks: Ownership shares in individual companies. Higher potential reward, higher risk when held alone. ETFs (exchange traded funds): Baskets of hundreds or thousands of stocks or bonds in a single purchase. The backbone of most beginner portfolios because they are diversified by design. Index funds: Funds that track a market benchmark such as the S&P 500 rather than trying to beat it. Low cost and historically difficult for active strategies to outperform over long periods. Bonds: Loans to companies or governments that pay interest. Generally lower risk than stocks and used to steady a portfolio. Cryptocurrencies: Digital assets available on some platforms, including Alinea, which offers access to more than 20 cryptocurrencies. Considered high risk and best kept to a small portion of a beginner portfolio, if any. How Beginner Investing Apps Compare Every major app handles the same basic workflow, but they differ in how much guidance they provide. Here is how the leading beginner platforms approach it. Choose a self directed app like Robinhood if you want full control and are willing to do your own research. Choose Acorns if passive spare change investing fits your habits. Choose Betterment if you want pure automation. Choose Alinea if you want automation plus education, expert built portfolios, and both AI and human guidance while you learn. 5 Mistakes Beginners Make on Investing Apps Investing money you may need soon. Keep an emergency fund in savings first. Invested money should have a multi year time horizon. Putting everything in one stock. Concentration is the fastest way to turn normal market movement into a painful loss. Diversified portfolios exist for a reason. Reacting to daily swings. Selling during a dip locks in losses. Historically, markets have moved through downturns and continued growing over long periods, though past performance never guarantees future results. Ignoring fees and fine print. Understand exactly what you pay, whether it is a subscription, a percentage of assets, or trading related costs, before you commit. Waiting for the perfect moment. Time in the market beats timing the market. Automated recurring investing makes the decision once so you never have to make it again. Frequently Asked Questions How much money do I need to start using an investment app? Very little. Fractional investing means most beginner apps let you start with a few dollars. On Alinea, you can begin investing with as little as $1. Starting small and contributing consistently matters far more than the size of your first deposit. Are investment apps safe for beginners? Regulated apps are built on the same protections as traditional brokerages. Look for SEC registration and SIPC protected brokerage accounts. Alinea is an SEC registered investment advisor, its brokerage accounts are powered by DriveWealth (member FINRA and SIPC) with protection up to $500,000, and it uses bank level 256-bit encryption. SIPC protects against brokerage failure, not market losses, which are a normal part of investing. How long does it take to set up an investment app account? Typically 10 to 15 minutes. Creating an account, completing the onboarding questionnaire, and linking a bank through Plaid are all done in app. Your first deposit may take one to a few business days to settle, after which you are fully invested. Do I need to know anything about the stock market first? No. Beginner focused apps are designed to be usable on day one. Expert built portfolios remove the need to research individual stocks, and tools like Alinea's AI Copilot Allie, daily briefings, and built in lessons teach you as you go, so your knowledge grows alongside your portfolio. What is the difference between a robo advisor and an app like Alinea? A robo advisor manages your money with an algorithm alone. Alinea takes a hybrid approach: portfolios are built by investment experts, automation handles the day to day, AI guidance explains everything in plain language, and human advisors are available for bigger financial questions. Beginners often prefer having a person to ask. Can I take my money out of an investment app? Yes. You can sell investments and withdraw funds to your linked bank account. Sales and transfers typically take a few business days to settle. Because investments fluctuate in value, withdrawing during a downturn may mean selling at a loss, which is one more reason to invest money you will not need short term. What should I invest in first as a complete beginner? Most financial educators point new investors toward broadly diversified portfolios of ETFs or index funds rather than individual stocks. Pre built options, like Alinea's Investment Playlists, package that diversification into a single choice aligned with your goals and risk tolerance. How often should I check my investment app? Weekly or monthly is plenty. Checking daily encourages emotional reactions to normal market movement. Set up automated contributions, review your progress on a schedule, and let time do the heavy lifting. Key Terms for New Investors Brokerage account: The account type that holds your investments and lets you buy and sell securities. Fractional shares: Partial pieces of a stock or ETF, letting you invest a dollar amount instead of buying whole shares. Diversification: Spreading investments across many companies and asset types to reduce the impact of any single one falling. Dollar cost averaging: Investing a fixed amount on a regular schedule regardless of market conditions. Compounding: When investment returns begin generating returns of their own, accelerating growth over time. Risk tolerance: How much short term fluctuation you can accept in pursuit of long term growth. SIPC protection: Insurance that protects brokerage account holders up to $500,000 if the brokerage fails. It does not cover market losses. Robo advisor: A platform that builds and manages a portfolio automatically using algorithms. Start Your Investing Journey With Alinea Using an investment app for the first time comes down to a handful of simple actions: choose a regulated platform, answer a few questions honestly, link your bank, start small, automate, and keep learning. Alinea was built to make each of those steps feel obvious, with expert built Investment Playlists, AI Copilot Allie, human advisor access, and a community of more than 2 million members. Download Alinea and make your first investment today, even if it is just $1. This content is for informational and educational purposes only and should not be construed as investment advice or a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Investing involves risk, including possible loss of principal. Past performance does not guarantee future results. Alinea is a registered investment advisor with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Brokerage accounts on Alinea are powered by DriveWealth, member FINRA and SIPC. title: USPS July 12, 2026 Price Change
summary: EasyPost - USPS July 12, 2026 Price Change %
body_text: USPS will be releasing a series of structural updates starting July 12, 2026 . Read our quick summary below to learn more about the coming changes. When will the new rates take effect? In November 2025, USPS migrated to a new time zone for all future price changes. Because of this, rate activation will take place at midnight Central Time (CT) instead of midnight Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). This also impacts future-dated shipments. Parcel dimensions required for all shipments Starting July 12, 2026, USPS requires length, width, and height on all commercial parcel manifests. As of this date, rating requests missing required dimensions will return an error. Dimensions required by container type: Parcel: all 3 dimensions SoftPack: all 3 dimensions Flat Rate, Letter, Card, Flat, PMOD: no dimensions required USPS Flat-Rate and USPS Returns shipments are exempt. USPS has deferred assessment of its Dimension Noncompliance fee until Phase Two (early 2027, tentative). New HazMat Handling and Non-Compliance Fees There will be two fees added related to HazMat shipments. HazMat Handling Fee: $7.50 charged for all packages containing HazMat Non-Compliance Fee: $50 charged per infraction for improperly labeled packages, including incorrect/missing STC, ESC, Service Icon or DOT marking Shippers and consumers will need to be cautious of the Non-Compliance Fee, as it could be triggered by reusing boxes with existing HazMat labeling or markers for non-HazMat labels. Updated Cubic tiers for Ground Advantage and Priority Mail Cubic tiers 0.6–1.0 will be removed. Cubic tiers 0.1–0.5 will receive new length + width measurements. The max length will increase from 18″ to 22″ for all cubic packages (boxes and soft-packs). See our table below to compare the tier changes. Tier Current Proposed 0.1 0″–16″ 0″–21″ 0.2 16″–21″ 21″–27″ 0.3 21″–24″ 27″–31″ 0.4 24″–26″ 31″–34″ 0.5 26″–28″ 34″–36″ 0.6–1.0 — Removed USPS Ground Advantage sub-pound rates unified for Commercial Pricing Commercial USPS Ground Advantage shipments to non-continental destinations will have unified sub-pound rates. For example a 4 oz. package and a 15.99 oz. package will be priced the same given all other details are equal. This impacts shipments to Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, and military addresses. Updated USPS Dimensional Weight Divisor USPS Dimensional Weight Divisor will change from 166 to 139. This aligns USPS’ common mail classes with the industry standard and ensures the price of the package more accurately represents the amount of space it takes in-transit. USPS will also implement a “Round Up” rule for all package dimensions. Any fraction of an inch will be rounded up to the next whole inch. Before July 12, 2026: LWH of (18.1”x12.1”x11.1”) would calculate to a value of 2400 in DIM On/After July 12, 2026: LWH of (18.1”x12.1”x11.1”) would calculate to a value of 3520 in DIM New Overweight/Oversize Item Fee NOTE: This fee will not impact EasyPost customers, as our API blocks oversize shipments. However, it is important to be aware that this fee will be implemented. USPS is implementing a new fee for packages 70 lbs or 130″ combined length + girth. This fee can be applied after manifest as well if USPS assesses the package is larger than marked.

title: The benefits of using a software-enabled electronics manufacturing service
summary: CircuitHub is a software based, full turn-key electronics manufacturing platform. We offer PCB assembly services, based in the US, while serving customers worldwide. body_text: ‍ CircuitHub is a software based, full turn-key electronics manufacturing platform. We offer PCB assembly services, based in the US, while serving customers worldwide. Now you might ask — "There are many other US PCB manufacturers available. What sets CircuitHub apart?" The main difference between CircuitHub and other Contract Manufacturers (CMs) in the market is the technology behind CircuitHub that powers it. This article highlights some of the main factors differentiate us from other existing PCB manufacturing solutions. ‍ We work with original EDA files Most manufacturers still only accept Gerber and BOM files. CircuitHub is one of the few CMs that reliably works solely using original EDA design files. While Gerber is a very well known format for transmitting manufacturing data to your manufacturer, there are less well understood downsides. Although some limited automated analysis of Gerber data is possible, the majority of CMs require you to manually provide them with additional information not captured in the Gerbers. This can slow down process, and is ultimately unnecessary since your EDA files usually contains all of this information in one form or another. We believe your time is much better spent focusing on your design itself rather than the logistics of getting it made. EDA files provide an almost perfect picture of your circuit board and assembly. By relying on these files CircuitHub is able to make sure you get precisely what you ordered with no unnecessary interruptions or distractions. ‍ Instant and accurate online quotes Since CircuitHub accepts original EDA files, getting a quote is as easy as dropping your files into your web browser. Our system extracts all the necessary BOM, bare board, and assembly information directly from your design files. Within minutes you will be given an accurate quote that is order ready. Although many CMs provide a way to get an online quote, most of these quotes require review by a human to ensure that they are accurate. These reviews are usually done through tedious and time consuming emails and phone calls. We go into more depth on how our instant quoting differs from the industry standard in this post . ‍ Our issue tracking system The standard mode of communication in the electronics manufacturing industry is email and phone calls. This often leaves you multiple steps away from the production team, resulting in poor issue management, wasted time, and more manufacturing errors. CircuitHub solves this problem with our issue tracking system that connects you directly to the relevant team members assembling your boards. There is no more "broken telephone" effect caused by messages being passed back and forth across different company divisions. Organizing and capturing all of these unstructured communications in one place allows us to maintain an audit trail and make sure that everyone is always on the same page. Additionally, this purpose-built system allows us to respond to order related queries in a timely manner. This is challenging for any manufacturer dealing with day-to-day manufacturing operations while simultaneously managing internal and external communications. ‍ Rapid prototyping CircuitHub offers affordable pricing at very fast and competitive lead times, enabling you to go from design to functioning prototype in as little as three working days. We know that the period spent waiting for a prototype to come back is, more often than not, time spent twiddling your thumbs. Our platform is designed to help you rapidly iterate on designs, eliminate wasted time, and accelerate your time to market. ‍ Scalable manufacturing CircuitHub is one of few manufacturers that can manufacture boards of a wide range of complexities from quantities 1 to 10,000. This allows you to test and finalize your design and then place an order for your larger production runs, without having to repeat the process with another manufacturer. Look out for improvements in the near future that will help make scaling to production even easier! ‍ Continuous, rapid innovation Rather than being a traditional manufacturer, at our core we are a technology company. Being software-based allows us to innovate, rather than relying only on processes and equipment to get the job done. We are continuously making changes that not only improve our manufacturing services, but also provides our customers with the best possible experience. A couple of things we are currently working on include accepting more EDA file formats, improved quoting, and expanding our production capabilities. ‍ If you're interested in learning more about how our software platform works, a good place to get started is our how it works page. Feel free to reach out to us if you'd like to speak to someone directly, or to set up a demo. ‍ Ready to try out CircuitHub for yourself? Sign up and upload a project now ! ‍ ‍

title: How to Make Facebook Ads Work For Your Small Business in 2023
summary: Maximize success with Facebook ads. Our 2023 guide helps e-commerce businesses gain a competitive edge in a cost-effective way. Create impactful campaigns
body_text: Facebooks advertising tool has become the preferred platform for many e-commerce business owners and marketers who want an affordable way to advertise their business online—especially those who are just starting out or have limited budgets to work with.
